response.justification: The candidate is an accomplished senior full-stack/web engineer with nearly two decades of software experience, but the role demands deep expertise in SoC/IP modeling, computer architecture, AI accelerator performance analysis, and hardware-software co-design — none of which appear in the resume. His background centers on web platforms (TypeScript, Node.js, DLang), with only tangential systems-level exposure (low-latency services, brief C/C++ work at National Instruments). There is no evidence of GPU/SIMD/MIMD architecture work, deep-learning workload optimization, or silicon-adjacent performance engineering, making this a poor fit for a Principal Performance Architect position.
strengths: 20+ years of software engineering experience, satisfying formal experience thresholds
Some low-latency, high-throughput systems experience (async I/O, fibers, caching at Dunnhumby)
Strong self-directed learner with open-source contributions and teaching/workshop experience
concerns: No SoC/IP modeling, computer architecture, or hardware-software co-design experience
No deep-learning training/inference optimization or GPU workload analysis background
Career trajectory is web/full-stack product engineering, not principal-level performance architecture

key_factors.factor: General systems and low-latency engineering exposure
